title: Too big to be ignored: how energy poverty undermines productive efficiency
summary: The large literature on the drivers of productive efficiency has not considered energy poverty, even though it affects efficiency on several fronts. This paper finds that energy poverty negatively affects productive efficiency.
keyFindings: Energy poverty negatively affects productive efficiency.
The negative effect persists across regions and is not sensitive to cross-country differences in income level.
The effect is more pronounced at higher levels of productive efficiency.
